SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What do we call describing where a county is by naming the places around it? (1 mark)
   A. Scale
   B. Rainfall
   C. Relative location
   D. Population

2. Which is the smallest county in Kenya by area? (1 mark)
   A. Turkana
   B. Kitui
   C. Mombasa
   D. Narok

3. What is a plain? (1 mark)
   A. Wide flat land
   B. A steep mountain
   C. A waterfall
   D. A lake with salt water

4. Why are mountains important for water? (1 mark)
   A. They make the land flat
   B. They dry up lakes
   C. They stop all rain
   D. They catch rain and give rise to rivers

5. If there is no pavement, which side of the road should a pedestrian walk on? (1 mark)
   A. The side with traffic behind
   B. In the middle of the road
   C. The side facing the oncoming traffic
   D. On the side where there is no light

6. Why should a weather chart be filled in at the same time each day? (1 mark)
   A. So that the chart looks big
   B. So that the sun rises earlier
   C. So that rain stops
   D. So that the records can be compared fairly

7. Which monument in Nairobi remembers Kenya's independence in 1963? (1 mark)
   A. Fort Jesus
   B. Thimlich Ohinga
   C. Uhuru Gardens
   D. Lamu Fort

8. What is a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. A bank
   B. A hospital
   C. A place for repairing cars
   D. A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive

9. Which is the best source of information about a historic place near you? (1 mark)
   A. A resource person such as an elder or a guide
   B. A rumour
   C. A guess
   D. An advert for soap

10. What might happen if all drivers stopped working? (1 mark)
   A. Schools would close forever
   B. Food and medicine could not reach shops and hospitals
   C. Nothing would change
   D. More crops would grow

11. What is one benefit of interdependence? (1 mark)
   A. We stop trading
   B. We get goods and services we cannot make ourselves
   C. We stop working
   D. We become poor

12. Which of these is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A bag of maize
   B. Treatment by a nurse
   C. A book
   D. A pair of shoes

13. Which group depends on teachers? (1 mark)
   A. Only farmers
   B. Only teachers
   C. Only drivers
   D. Everyone who wants to learn

14. What is population? (1 mark)
   A. The rainfall in a place
   B. The size of a place
   C. The number of people living in a place
   D. The number of animals in a place

15. Which cloth is a printed cloth worn especially at the Kenyan coast? (1 mark)
   A. Suit
   B. Jeans
   C. Shuka
   D. Kanga

16. Which is a good school rule? (1 mark)
   A. Fight in class
   B. Come to school on time
   C. Break desks
   D. Write on walls

17. Keeping cattle, goats and camels in dry areas is called what? (1 mark)
   A. Mining
   B. Pastoralism
   C. Fishing
   D. Trading

18. Reduce, reuse and recycle are ways of doing what? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting down waste
   B. Drying fish
   C. Growing tea
   D. Building roads

19. What is a factory? (1 mark)
   A. A large building where goods are made with machines
   B. A market
   C. A hospital
   D. A school

20. Which colour is best for a road safety bib? (1 mark)
   A. Dark brown
   B. Black
   C. Grey
   D. Bright orange or yellow

21. Which of these is a viable project? (1 mark)
   A. One that is dangerous
   B. One that people want, is safe and can earn more than it costs
   C. One that costs more than it earns
   D. One that nobody wants

22. What is personal protective equipment used for? (1 mark)
   A. To slow down work
   B. To make noise
   C. To protect a person from harm
   D. To hide

23. A group spent Ksh 600 and earned Ksh 500. What happened? (1 mark)
   A. A loss of Ksh 100
   B. A profit of Ksh 1,100
   C. No change
   D. A profit of Ksh 100

24. Which behaviour shows patriotism? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring the flag
   B. Standing respectfully during the national anthem
   C. Laughing during the anthem
   D. Damaging public property

25. What does listening do for peace? (1 mark)
   A. It starts fights
   B. It wastes time
   C. It helps people to understand each other
   D. It makes people angry

26. Two pupils want the same ball. What is a peaceful solution? (1 mark)
   A. Fight for it
   B. Hide it
   C. Take turns to play with it
   D. Break it

27. Which of these is a trusted adult? (1 mark)
   A. A person who threatens you
   B. A person who gives you sweets in secret
   C. A parent or teacher
   D. A stranger you met online

28. Which of these is a child right? (1 mark)
   A. To be married early
   B. To be beaten
   C. To go to school
   D. To work in a quarry

29. What is a mock election? (1 mark)
   A. A school holiday
   B. A practice election
   C. A real national election
   D. A game with no rules

30. Why do we have county governments? (1 mark)
   A. To stop elections
   B. To end services
   C. To close schools
   D. To bring services closer to the people

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how your class could showcase its school enterprise project. (5 marks)

32. Explain how citizens can support the county government. (4 marks)

33. Give two ways in which Mount Kenya is useful. (2 marks)

34. Explain why discipline is important in school. (3 marks)

35. Explain what an industry is. (2 marks)

36. Explain the difference between the governor and the president. (3 marks)

37. Explain why a mountain can be a source of water for people living far away. (3 marks)

38. A pupil stands facing east. Say what is behind the pupil, on the left and on the right. (3 marks)

39. Explain the difference between a chief and a clan elder. (3 marks)

40. State three causes of child abuse in a community. (3 marks)

41. Describe four things a school can do to promote child rights. (4 marks)

42. Explain the difference between a right and a duty and give one example of each in school. (4 marks)

43. State three ways in which physical features are important to people. (3 marks)

44. Explain why some cultural practices are no longer kept. (3 marks)

45. Give three reasons why historic built environments are important. (3 marks)

46. Name two historic places in Kenya and the town or county where each is found. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Relative location
   Relative location compares a place with its neighbours.

2. C — Mombasa
   Mombasa covers the smallest area of all the counties.

3. A — Wide flat land
   A plain is a wide, flat area.

4. D — They catch rain and give rise to rivers
   Mountains catch rain and feed rivers.

5. C — The side facing the oncoming traffic
   Facing traffic lets you see vehicles coming towards you.

6. D — So that the records can be compared fairly
   Observing at the same time gives fair comparisons.

7. C — Uhuru Gardens
   Uhuru Gardens is where the Kenyan flag was first raised at independence.

8. D — A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive
   Cultural centres show dances, homes, crafts and foods.

9. A — A resource person such as an elder or a guide
   Elders and guides know the true story of the place.

10. B — Food and medicine could not reach shops and hospitals
   Transport connects producers, shops and hospitals.

11. B — We get goods and services we cannot make ourselves
   Sharing skills gives us more goods and services.

12. B — Treatment by a nurse
   A service is work done for someone. The others are goods.

13. D — Everyone who wants to learn
   Teachers help children learn to read and write, which everybody needs.

14. C — The number of people living in a place
   Population is the number of people in an area.

15. D — Kanga
   The kanga is printed cloth popular on the coast.

16. B — Come to school on time
   Being punctual is a good habit.

17. B — Pastoralism
   Pastoralism is keeping livestock on natural pasture.

18. A — Cutting down waste
   The three Rs cut down waste.

19. A — A large building where goods are made with machines
   Factories use machines to make goods.

20. D — Bright orange or yellow
   Bright colours are easy to see.

21. B — One that people want, is safe and can earn more than it costs
   Viable means it can work.

22. C — To protect a person from harm
   PPE protects the wearer.

23. A — A loss of Ksh 100
   They spent more than they earned: 600 - 500 = 100.

24. B — Standing respectfully during the national anthem
   Respecting national symbols shows love for the country.

25. C — It helps people to understand each other
   Listening helps solve conflicts.

26. C — Take turns to play with it
   Taking turns is fair.

27. C — A parent or teacher
   Trusted adults protect children.

28. C — To go to school
   Children have the right to education.

29. B — A practice election
   A mock election teaches how voting works.

30. D — To bring services closer to the people
   Counties bring services near to people.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Set up a stall with the goods, display a poster, show records of costs and income, explain each team member's role, and let visitors ask questions and give feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Attend public meetings, vote, pay fees and taxes, and take care of public property.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: It gives water for rivers and it attracts tourists. Accept rich soils for farming.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the school orderly, it helps everyone learn, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: An industry is a place or business where raw materials are made into goods, or where a service is given to many people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for making goods, 1 mark for services or raw materials.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: The president leads the national government of the whole country. The governor leads one county government.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mountains catch rain. The rain flows into rivers. Rivers carry the water to farms and towns far away.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind is west. On the left is north. On the right is south.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct direction.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: A chief is appointed by the national government to lead a location. A clan elder is respected by a clan for age and wisdom and keeps customs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Poverty, harmful beliefs and lack of knowledge of the law. Accept greed or conflict.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cause.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make posters, sing songs on child protection, set up a suggestion box, and include all children in activities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: A right is something you are allowed, such as learning in a safe place. A duty is something you must do, such as following the rules.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give water, they provide fish and food, and they attract visitors. Accept farming land or electric power.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some practices harm people, such as female genital mutilation and early marriage. The law forbids them. We keep the good parts and leave out the harmful ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harm, 1 mark for law, 1 mark for keeping good parts.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: They teach us history, they give us identity and pride, and they bring tourists and income.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fort Jesus in Mombasa and Thimlich Ohinga in Migori County. Accept Lamu Old Town or Gede Ruins.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct place with its location.
